title: Describe projective bundles by finite exterior modules
statement: Can algebraic vector bundles on \(\mathbb P^n\) be represented and compared by finite-dimensional graded modules over an exterior algebra? The notebook's broad classification question is indexed in the specific form answered by its theorem.
status: As of November 2026, the representation and stable-isomorphism criterion are established by BGG. A full explicit moduli classification is a different, substantially broader question and is not claimed solved here.

title: Why homogeneous functions define a line bundle
statement: Why do homogeneous rational functions of integer degree \(j\), regular above a projective open set, form a locally free sheaf of rank one?
status: Resolved classically: division by \(x_i^j\) gives an explicit local trivialization on \(x_i\ne0\). This is an exercise, not an open research question.

title: Cohomology of the integral formal substitution group
statement: Compute the cohomology of \(J=\{t+\sum_{i\ge1}a_it^{i+1}:a_i\in\mathbb Z\}\). The notebook leaves coefficients and topology unstated. This chapter distinguishes finite-jet cohomology \(\varinjlim_NH^*(J/(t^{N+1});A)\), continuous cochains, and unrestricted cohomology of the abstract group.
status: As of November 2026, Babenko--Bogatyi's real uniformly locally constant-support theory is computed and its continuous abelianization is known. For the explicit integral finite-jet refinement, the chapter derives torsion \((\mathbb Z/2)^2\) in degree two and a vanishing product of the two integral degree-one generators. It does not compute the full integral ring or the abstract discrete theory. Pavez-Cornejo's 2024 preprint/2025 publication uses closed commutators, not ordinary abstract commutators.
